advantages.what: A 64-character agent name is accepted and the ticket's assignee becomes that name; a 65-character name is refused and the assignee is left unchanged. Y's limit is 63, so a name the request allows is rejected.

lesser_lacks: Change the assignee maximum from 63 characters to 64, so a 64-character name is stored and only 65 or more is refused without changing the ticket.
pairs.why: On every audited path except name length, Y and Z assign, unassign, notify, filter, audit, and persist the same way, and they share the same document, UTF-8, and test gaps. Y fails the stated 64-character rule because its limit is 63. That single constant is the gap.

advantages.what: The new behaviour is tested once, in test/assignment.test.js. X also ships test/assignment-again.test.js, a copy with renamed tests that adds no check and must be edited in step with the original.
No specification file was added. X's docs/spec.md restates the request six times and records none of the choices the code makes, so a maintainer still has to read the code for the contract.

pairs.why: X and Z run the same feature, including a correct 64-character limit, and the shared defects do not separate them. X adds a duplicate of the new tests and a specification that decides nothing. Z leaves one test file and no empty spec for the maintainer to carry.

advantages.what: A 64-character agent name is accepted and a 65-character name is refused with the ticket unchanged. Y refuses the 64-character name because its limit is 63.
The new tests live in one file. X also ships test/assignment-again.test.js, a renamed copy that adds no check and has to stay in step on every test change.
No specification document was added. X's docs/spec.md repeats the request and does not record the behaviour the code chose.

lesser_lacks: Change the assignee maximum from 63 characters to 64, so a 64-character name is stored and only 65 or more is refused without changing the ticket.
pairs.why: X meets the stated 64-character rule and Y does not; that is the only behavioural difference between them. Y is lighter to keep because its tests are not duplicated and it adds no empty specification. A wrong limit on a stated rule outweighs that maintenance cost, and changing the constant removes it.
